# Standup Notes Template (the four-section contract)

Canonical structure for a standup digest under `knowledge/meetings/`. The
`ingest-standup` command writes to this shape. The four section headings are
the contract -- keep the heading text byte-identical wherever a digest lives,
so downstream steps (the meetings index, the standups log) can find each part
by name.

---

## Frontmatter block

Every standup digest opens with this YAML frontmatter:

```yaml
---
date: YYYY-MM-DD
type: meeting
meeting_kind: standup
title: Short meeting title
source: meetings/raw/<slug>.<ext>
attendees: [Name One, Name Two]
duration_min: NN
---
```

## Summary

One overall paragraph or a handful of bullets: what the meeting was about and
where it landed. This is the section other steps quote from -- the meetings
index one-liner and the standups log highlights both draw from here, so keep
it self-contained.

```
## Summary

<what the meeting covered and where it landed, 2-5 sentences or bullets>
```

## Action items

What came out of the meeting. A markdown table, one row per item, each row
traceable to a specific transcript cue. Due is `TBD` unless a date was
stated in the meeting; convert any relative date ("next Tuesday") to an
absolute one.

```
## Action items

| Item | Owner | Due | Source cue |
|------|-------|-----|-------------|
| <concrete task> | <name> | <YYYY-MM-DD or TBD> | <cue reference> |
```

Write "None" if the meeting produced no action items. Do not invent a due
date that was not stated.

## Questions / decisions

Split into two subsections. A decision names an owner; a question does not
need one until it is resolved.

```
## Questions / decisions

### Decisions

- <decision>, owner: <name>

### Questions

- <open question, unresolved as of this meeting>
```

Write "None" under a subhead with no content.

## Follow-ups

What needs to happen next and who owns it. Distinct from Action items --
Action items are discrete tasks that came out of this meeting; Follow-ups
are what happens as a result, often spanning beyond one person's next task
(a check-in, a re-review, a dependency to watch).

Blockers live here. There is no separate Blockers section. Write a blocked
item as a Follow-up, say what it is waiting on, and name the owner who can
unblock it.

```
## Follow-ups

- <what happens next>, owner: <name>
```

Write "None" if there is nothing forward-looking beyond the action items.

All four sections always render. A section with nothing in it says "None"
rather than being dropped, so a reader can tell an empty section from a
missed one.

---

## Full skeleton

```
---
date: YYYY-MM-DD
type: meeting
meeting_kind: standup
title: <title>
source: meetings/raw/<slug>.<ext>
attendees: [<names>]
duration_min: <NN>
---

# <title> -- <date>

## Summary

<summary>

## Action items

| Item | Owner | Due | Source cue |
|------|-------|-----|-------------|
| <item> | <owner> | <due or TBD> | <cue> |

## Questions / decisions

### Decisions

- <decision>, owner: <name>

### Questions

- <question>

## Follow-ups

- <follow-up>, owner: <name>
```
